name: solid FeS

Heng, "Optical properties of potential condensates in exoplanetary atmospheres", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 475 (2018) 94–107, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stx3141
source: Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation (D. Kitzmann and K. Heng, "Optical properties of potential condensates in exoplanetary atmospheres", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 475 (2018) 94–107, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stx3141), LX-MIE's compilation/FeS.dat at commit 38cc6d97c2268d58c41ccfc3955283ab6ee2ca44, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NewStrangeWorlds/LX-MIE/38cc6d97c2268d58c41ccfc3955283ab6ee2ca44/compilation/FeS.dat, SHA-256 ae2ba0daab33afc92d2d7590b1712cf7c09a35f8465915b19ab501396c4d60ea, fetched 2026-10-14; read as data, as the only machine-readable copy of its primary
licence: reduced values from Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation, the only machine-readable copy found, cited to the primary and to Kitzmann and Heng as the compiler: the measured values are the authors' facts, and the repository's GPL-3.0 covers its code and arrangement, not a reduced visible subset of one material; its compilation/readme.txt sets no separate terms for the data. No compilation file and none of LX-MIE's code is committed (decision-composition §5; decision-r08-licences.md)
reduction: n linear and k linear in log k in wavelength between the source's rows, onto 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures. The source's rows near the visible are 300, 460, 610 and 1,000 nm, so 380–780 nm is interpolated across them, as coarse as the source; the visible primary, Pollack et al. 1994, was not found in another machine-readable copy (the Jena database's FeS is infrared only). The copy states no temperature
